company_name: Defense Logistics Agency Strategic Materials (National Defense Stockpile)
parent_company: Defense Logistics Agency (US Department of Defense / Department of War)
tie_detail: Origin of legacy NDS inventory lots (e.g., tungsten ores and concentrates, germanium) is not published. FY2026 acquisitions favour domestic/allied sources (Elmet tungsten, Atalco Louisiana gallium, GAM Boyertown tantalum ingot) but the Glencore cobalt IDIQ source mine/refinery is not disclosed.
products: Seller of excess and buyer for the NDS. FY2025 Annual Materials Plan potential DISPOSALS: tungsten ores & concentrates 499 t W content; germanium 5,000 kg gross; tantalum metal 0.09 t. FY2025 potential ACQUISITIONS: tungsten 2,041 t; tantalum metal 29.26 t; cobalt alloys 60 t; NdPr oxide 300 t; NdFeB magnet block 450 t; SmCo alloy 60 t; lanthanum 1,100 t. FY2026 IDIQ buys: tungsten ores/concentrates/sodium tungstate, gallium, cobalt, nickel, high-purity aluminium, antimony ingot, tantalum ingot. USGS MCS 2026: molybdenum stockpile 'None'; gallium stockpile 'Not available'.
facility_name: DLA Strategic Materials HQ (NDS storage depots nationwide)
feedstock_origin: Legacy inventory of unpublished origin; new contracts target domestic and allied supply (see committed_offtakes).
committed_offtakes: DLA as BUYER under IDIQs (ceilings, not guaranteed): Elmet Technologies tungsten ores/concentrates/sodium tungstate up to $2B, $150M minimum, 5 yr from 11 Sep 2026; Glencore cobalt up to $900M over 5 yr (awarded May 2026); Atlantic Alumina (Atalco) gallium up to $350M / 55,610 kg over 5 yr; Glencore nickel up to $65M; tantalum ingot delivery order $8.6M (Sep 2025) plus 5-yr contract up to $100M to the Boyertown PA tantalum processor; US Antimony up to $245M (2025).
government_awards: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Jul 2025): $2B for NDS purchases, available through FY2029; DLA reports $2B committed in FY2026 (announced 5 Nov 2026).
dfars_7052_reason: Origin of legacy stockpile lots is not published; any NDS material bought for 2027-compliant use needs lot-level mine-to-metal origin records.
broker_fit_rationale: A channel rather than a partner: disposals are small (FY2025 AMP: 499 t W ores, 5,000 kg Ge; no FY2026 or FY2027 AMP published) and sold only to registered bidders via BOA/auction. DLA is now mainly a buyer, so it matters more as a customer for compliant supply.
sources: https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-tungsten.pdf; https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-tantalum.pdf; https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-germanium.pdf; https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-rare-earths.pdf; https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2026/mcs2026-cobalt.pdf; https://www.northernminer.com/news/us-reports-2b-in-mineral-stockpile-commitments/1003897547/; https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news-and-insights/latest-market-news/2903231-us-aims-to-grow-mineral-stockpile; https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/dod-war-elmet-group-tungsten-supply-chain-dla-economic-defense-unit/830331/; https://www.dla.mil/Portals/104/Documents/Strategic Materials/Solicitation Docs/DLA-Stockpile Materials-001_BOA_FINAL POSTING COPY.pdf; https://www.dla.mil/Portals/104/Documents/Strategic Materials/Announcements/3273 BOA All September 2025 Sales.pdf; https://www.dla.mil/Portals/104/Documents/Strategic Materials/Announcements/3252 BOA All June 2024 Sales.pdf
notes: Sales method: standing solicitation DLA-Stockpile Materials-001 (Basic Ordering Agreement version issued 3 Jul 2017, plus an auction version). Buyers register once; the Stockpile Sales Officer issues an acceptance letter; registered firms then bid on monthly BOA offerings, with results posted monthly (e.g., ferrochrome, chromium metal, tin in 2024-2025; tungsten ores & concentrates sold in Mar 2023). USGS MCS 2026: 'For fiscal year 2026, the Annual Materials Plan was not released.' Argus (Nov 2026): no FY2027 AMP yet. DLA website blocks automated fetches; sales details are from search snippets of DLA documents. The cancelled Aug 2025 cobalt tender (7,480 t, $500M ceiling) was replaced by the Glencore award.

company_name: VaultCo LLC (Project Vault - U.S. Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve)
parent_company: Independently governed public-private partnership of OEMs and private capital providers
ultimate_owner: Participating OEMs and private capital providers (EXIM is lender and non-controlling board observer)
tie_detail: No sourcing or origin rules published (Fastmarkets, Oct 2026). The first reported physical delivery (Mercuria, week of 15 Oct 2026) was 12,000 t of DRC copper; Gecamines ships US-bound copper from its 20% share of Tenke Fungurume, which is 80% owned by China's CMOC.
products: Reserve of critical minerals for participating US manufacturers; OEM requests reportedly extend to specific magnets, powders and alloys (VaultCo chair, Oct 2026). Commitments so far: Glencore $500M (cobalt) and Mercuria $500M (23 Sep 2026). Minerals list, volumes and storage sites undisclosed.
facility_name: Storage facilities across the United States (locations undisclosed)
expected_production_date: First delivery Oct 2026; first OEM loan tranche (~$1B, >12 firms) planned Q4 2026
feedstock_origin: Procured globally by trader participants (Glencore, Mercuria, Hartree Partners, Traxys); origin rules not disclosed.
committed_offtakes: Suppliers named Feb 2026: Hartree Partners, Mercuria Americas, Traxys; Glencore and Mercuria $500M each (23 Sep 2026). OEMs named: Clarios, GE Vernova, Western Digital, Boeing (EXIM); later reports add Corning, GM, Google, Stellantis.
government_awards: EXIM direct loan up to $10B approved 2 Feb 2026 (plus ~$1.67-2B private capital); EXIM 'Deal of the Year' (May 2026).
dfars_7052_reason: No origin rules are published; compliance depends on each lot's mine-to-metal chain, which VaultCo does not disclose.
broker_fit_rationale: A demand-side channel for clients that join as OEM participants, not a stock source for brokers. Access requires up-front fees and a commitment to buy at a set inventory price plus carrying cost; origin rules are undisclosed.
notes: Separate from the DLA National Defense Stockpile; EO 14415 sec. 6 states the order does not affect Project Vault. Mechanism (Oct 2026 reports): manufacturers pay up-front fees, commit to buy material later at a specified inventory price, and pay carrying costs (interest and storage); drawdown decisions rest with manufacturers. VaultCo withholds purchase quantities to avoid moving small markets and says it is in talks with >70 firms. Executive Chairman named publicly (role only recorded here).

First (preliminary) deal: up to 500 t/yr rare earths (oxide) from Arafura's Nolans project.

notes: Miners asked for a price collar for rare earths (S&P, Jan 2026). Government DISR page returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-16; facts from Reuters/trade press. Arafura site preparation expected Sept 2026, construction ~3 years.

company_name: Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) - national rare metals stockpile
parent_company: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
tie_detail: Stockpile composition, quantities and origin are undisclosed (IEA). Japan still sources most rare earths from China (Adnkronos, Jan 2026), so the origin of stockpiled lots cannot be assumed non-China.

Target generally 60 days of national consumption, up to ~180 days for high-geopolitical-risk minerals. JOGMEC also co-invests in non-China supply (e.g., up to C$47.7M in Toyota Tsusho's Namibian rare earth project, Jul 2026).
government_awards: n/a (government agency); stockpile funded by interest subsidies and warehouse cost support
dfars_7052_reason: Origin of stockpiled lots is undisclosed and releases go to Japanese industry, not to US defense buyers.
broker_fit_rationale: Releases serve Japanese domestic users in supply emergencies; no evidence of sales to foreign intermediaries. Useful as a co-investor signal in non-China projects, not as a stock source.
notes: Japan sought G7 price floors and proposed joint critical-minerals stockpiling in 2026 (press headlines). JOGMEC stockpile pages returned HTTP 503 on 2026-11-16.
